moods.title: What to See at the Marché Central
moods.subtitle: Seafood, spices and everyday shopping — three faces of the market.

1.title: Fish & Seafood Counters
1.desc: The busiest section: fresh catch from the Atlantic, sold by the kilo to locals and cooks.

2.title: Spice & Produce Aisles
2.desc: Spices, olives, fruit and vegetables — a true working market, not a tourist stage.

3.title: Flower Stalls
3.desc: Colour and scent at the edge of the market — good for photos and a short pause.

q1.question: Is Marché Central free?
q1.answer: Yes for the market streets; the church is usually free or by donation.

q3.question: When is best?
q3.answer: Morning for the market; daytime for stained glass.

q5.question: What to combine with?
q5.answer: Place Mohammed V, Old Medina, or Villa des Arts.

food.title: What to Eat at and Near the Marché Central
food.p1: This is a working market. You come for produce and seafood; simple eateries nearby handle sit-down meals.
food.li1: Fresh seafood at the market counters.
food.li4: Downtown restaurants a few blocks away.
food.li5: Spice and olive purchases if shopping.
food.p2: Go in the morning. For a sit-down meal, step outside the hall.
